### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAutomationRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f26456e3029716056fc58c7cf3c16345b1f3f99b` — the merge of head `62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed` into base `3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f26456e3029716056fc58c7cf3c16345b1f3f99b && git checkout f26456e3029716056fc58c7cf3c16345b1f3f99b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1 62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1 && git merge --no-ff 62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b1307ede47aa09653af8cea1295df217c4c44f1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — FAIL (L1; this head is not landable)

Head-sha: `62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed`
Reviewer: review-c · read 2026-11-16T07:58Z · first round, L1 only; claim 6910311824
Implemented-by: `claude/area-A5b-34145` · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

**The L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is not on this head.** The review tier was unavailable for both runs, so no record was posted. On the seat's ruling, this L1 goes first so the fix can start. The L2 record will be written on the fixed head once the tier is back.

**What holds:** the direction. The four write doors now ask the engine's durable key rule rather than the served read, which makes ADR-0150 D3's refusal real at the write doors. Neither half of the change hands a caller a body or a credential it could not read before.

**Owed:**
1. **F1: the declared narrowing is pinned nowhere.** The `!`, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and R2 all rest on one row. A package-less `PUT /automation/NAME` or `POST /automation` onto a name two packages hold, after the disabled co-holder's slot was withdrawn, in a composition with no metadata store, now answers `409` where it answered `200`.
   - The new runtime file has no shared-name `PUT` or `POST /` case. Its shared-name cases are clone and `DELETE` only, and every rig supplies `saveMetaItem`, so the no-store composition is never built.
   - The engine-side pin went into the disabled-sole-holder case. The `[#33893]` withdrawn-slot block gained no `getHeldFlow` assertion.
   - **Fix:** add one `getHeldFlow` assertion in the withdrawn-slot case, and one no-store rig driving `PUT` and `POST /` onto the shared name.
2. **F2: the BREAKING remedy cannot be applied where the banner says it bites.** The banner is scoped to a composition with no metadata store, but its remedy is the metadata door with `?package=`, which needs one. The addressed write doors deliberately keep their own `409`.
   - **Fix:** name a remedy that exists there (for example, uninstalling the co-holder folds the name back), and say plainly that otherwise the write is refused there exactly as while both holders are enabled.
3. **F3: one release would publish two contradictory accounts.** `.changeset/33905-disabled-sole-holder-flow.md` (from #34048, still pending on `main`) has a BREAKING block, "Three HTTP write doors ask `getFlow` whether the name is held". It says the clone door lets the copy through, the put-back withdraws the name, a `PUT` drops the stored credential and `DELETE` answers `404`. This PR reverses all four before either entry ships.
   - **Fix:** correct the #33905 changeset in this PR. Both entries are pending, so it is a prose face of this release.

**Nit:** the shape of the clone door's shared-name refusal changes from a returned answer to a thrown one, with the same status and code. Either state it, or catch the refusal into the door's own path.

**Checks:** 55 check-runs, 37 success and 18 skipped, none red.

Not governed: the area lands this PR once L1 and the L2 record both read clean.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-write-doors-durable-34145.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-dispatch-status.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (cited code, read on `main`, not reviewed); .changeset/34145-write-doors-durable-read.md judged for ② only
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the net diff against `main` and the cited code; nothing run. Check-runs on this head: 37 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed.

What the diff does: four reads in `automation.ts` (clone new-name probe, `registerAndSaveFlow` put-back copy `held`, `keepStoredFlowCredentials`, `unregisterAndDeleteFlow` existence probe) move from `getFlow` (served: `servedBareFlowKey`) to a new `AutomationEngine.getHeldFlow` (`bareFlowKey`: every holder, a shared name thrown 409). A service without `getHeldFlow` is asked `getFlow` as before.

- Disabled sole holder (name held by one package, package disabled, slot held). RIGHT as stated. `bareFlowKey` returns the name when `flowSlots.isShared` is false, so `getHeldFlow` answers the slot body where `getFlow` answers `null`. Clone onto the name: admitted on `main`, now the door's name-taken 409. Put-back: body re-registered instead of withdrawn. `PUT` without the secret: stored secret carried. `DELETE`: 200 instead of 404. Each is the last release's answer (#34048 is unreleased), so none is a narrowing against the release. Enabled holder, unknown name, slot-key spelling: unchanged (both reads agree).
- `DELETE` on a shared name: RIGHT, unchanged. `unregisterFlow` already threw the same refusal through `bareFlowKey`; it is now thrown one line earlier.
- Definition writes on a shared name while the disabled holder's slot is still held: RIGHT, status unchanged (409). `main` returned `placeFlowSlot`'s refusal from `registerFlow`; the head throws it from `keepStoredFlowCredentials` before anything is read or registered.
- Definition writes on a shared name after the disabled holder's slot was withdrawn (one slot under its qualified key, registry still holds the name twice, so `isShared` is true): the PR states FROM "refused 409 by the store's package-less save, 200 only with no store". WRONG. On `main` `registerFlow` lands the body in the enabled holder's slot, and `saveMetaItem` naming no package is then addressed by `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` (protocol-save.ts, #32605) to the ENABLED holder's row: `servedAddressJudgment` answers `served` from the registry (`servedHolderAddressOf`), and failing that the stored bindings are judged over the enabled ones (`enabled.length === 1` is the address). The save is accepted. So FROM is 200 with the body stored in the enabled holder's row, in a composition WITH a metadata store, wherever the authoring rule admits the write; TO is 409 before anything is registered. The narrowing is not confined to a store-less composition. See M1.
- Same state with every holder disabled and one slot left: `main` `getFlow` is `null` and `registerFlow` lands in the remaining slot; the head refuses 409. Same class, not named by the PR ("one of them disabled").
- Clone onto a shared new name, one holder disabled: RIGHT on status (409 both sides), but the answer changes from the door's returned name-taken refusal to the engine's thrown `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`. See S2.
- `getHeldFlow` as a new public method on an exported class: RIGHT, a widening, declared in the changeset's Added line.
- Nothing else moves: the read and run doors and the clone's source probe keep `getFlow`.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/service-automation` beside `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct per AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: no authorable key, value or type changes, and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and ADR-0087 disposition.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is well-formed, present line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; title and changeset subject carry `!`; exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Check Changeset: success (both runs).
- The BREAKING banner is the changeset's FROM/TO and its one-line fix, and it ships as CHANGELOG. Its scope ("only for a composition with no metadata store") and the sentence "The store's save, which names no package, then refused it 409 naming the packages" are false against `main` (① row 4). Its remedy is written for the wrong composition. The ADR-0087 marker's reason repeats the same premise; the disposition itself (nothing stored moves) still holds. Must-fix, M1.
- S3: `.changeset/33905-disabled-sole-holder-flow.md`, pending on `main`, tells the same release that the clone door admits the copy, the put-back withdraws the name, `PUT` drops the credential and `DELETE` answers 404 for a disabled sole holder. This changeset says the opposite of all four. One release would publish both.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (is `getHeldFlow` a widening): the PR declares it a widening and cites "seat ruling on #34145 R1". open_questions 2 (the shared-name write): the PR declares a narrowing and cites "R2". Neither ruling is on #34145. Its comments are triage 6902701885, claim 6906301024, dev report 6908470345 and claim amendment 6908514753, and the amendment says the claim's `Clause-②: no` stands and the two readings "are with the seat". The claim of record therefore contradicts the PR and the changeset. S4. Question 2 is ESCALATED, not answered: the dev's option A and the R2 the PR describes both rest on the false "the store already refused it" premise (M1), so the question has to be ruled again on the facts in ①.
- Dev deviations: pins in a new file rather than a shared harness (the runtime automation domain has per-concern files; accepted); runtime dependents and repo lint left to CI (Test Core 8/8, lint lanes and Dogfood Regression Gate are success on this head); the 75-family sweep not re-run after test-only and changeset commits (the CI gate lanes are success on this head).
- Dogfood battery owed by the narrowing arm: Dogfood Regression Gate success.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The diff adds no query, id materialisation or per-holder loop; `getHeldFlow` is one in-memory map read behind `bareFlowKey`, and the holder count is the resolver's existing answer.
- Security: the `keepStoredFlowCredentials` hunk changes which stored credential a `PUT` carries forward (a disabled sole holder's secret is kept again). No caller gains a read: the door still answers `servedFlowDefinition`. Recorded `yes`.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — the narrowing takes a served capability away, and is declared on a false FROM. On `main` a package-less write to a flow name an enabled and a disabled package both hold is served by the enabled holder at every bare door that counts holders: the bare reads (`getFlow`, `servedBareFlowKey`, #33386), the engine's package-less registration once the disabled slot is withdrawn (`placeFlowSlot` judges `flowNameRefusal` on the served resolver, then takes the name's one slot), and the metadata protocol's package-less save (`servedPackagelessSaveAddress`, #32605, epic ruling 6781691009: "a disabled package holds nothing an address reaches, so it is never the address and never named"; its docblock lists "refused 409 naming the disabled package while the read served the enabled one" as the defect it removed). After this diff `PUT /automation/NAME` and `POST /automation` refuse that write 409 naming the disabled holder, while `PUT /meta/flow/NAME` with no package accepts it into the enabled holder's row and `GET /automation/NAME` serves that holder. "Judge a flow name over every holder" therefore does NOT agree with how holders are counted at the bare read and save doors; seat ruling 6884403301 amendment 7, as the engine cites it, keys slots, run keys and bindings over every holder and leaves the doors on the served set (amendment 9). The every-holder read is right for the disabled SOLE holder (the card's stated case) and is the over-reach for a shared name. It does make one thing consistent: the write is already refused while the disabled slot is still held, so `main` answers the same request differently before and after the re-sync. Which way to close that is a ruling, and it has not been made on true facts. Owed: (a) a ruling recorded on #34145, made on ① row 4 as read here, choosing between keeping the every-holder refusal at these doors (then the full narrowing is declared: with-store FROM 200 into the enabled holder's row, every-holder-disabled variant included, a remedy the caller can follow, the ADR-0087 reason corrected, and the disagreement with the #32605 save door ruled on) or reading the shared name on the served holder at the definition doors (the dev's option B, which leaves the sole-holder fix intact and no narrowing); (b) the PR body, the changeset and the marker rewritten to match. A reviewer or dev should confirm ① row 4 with one pin through the real protocol before the ruling; it is read here, not run.

S1 (should-fix) — the declared narrowing is pinned nowhere. The new runtime file has no shared-name `PUT` or `POST /` case (its shared-name cases are clone and `DELETE`), every rig is a double that supplies `saveMetaItem`, and the engine pin sits in the disabled-sole-holder case; the `[#33893]` withdrawn-slot block has no `getHeldFlow` assertion. Whatever M1's ruling, the row the `!` stands on needs a pin, one of them against the real save address.

S2 (should-fix) — the clone door's shared new-name answer regresses. `main` returned the door's own name-taken 409 with its remedy (pick a name no flow uses); `registerAndSaveFlow`'s own contract says a name two packages hold is TAKEN at the clone door. The head throws the engine refusal instead ("the caller names no package ... address it by its package"), a remedy a clone caller cannot follow, and the clone body's `package` key (the landing package) invites exactly the wrong reading. Catch the shared-name refusal at the probe and answer name-taken; that also covers the both-enabled case, which already threw on `main`.

S3 (should-fix) — the two pending changesets contradict each other (②). Correct the #33905 entry in this PR.

S4 (should-fix) — R1 and R2 are cited but not on the card, and the claim of record says `Clause-②: no` (③). Post the rulings and amend the claim.

N1 (nit) — `getHeldFlow` is a read that can re-key a slot (`settleFlowName`), as `getFlow` does; its docblock could say so.

Tried and held: disabled sole holder at all four doors; a name only a disabled package holds through clone, put-back, credential carry and `DELETE`; slot-key spelling (`null` on both reads); a service with neither read (`DELETE` never "unknown", as before); put-back keeps the held body's arm (`flowArms`); the read-then-register window is the one `main` already had and no longer depends on enable state.
